summary: Baker County L-4 lookout on the Wallowa-Whitman NF, first manned 1939; cab dated 1949 by NHLR (1937 by others), staffed summers, and still standing after the 2016 Rail Fire.

facts.design: 14 x 14 ft L-4 ground cab with catwalk (present cab dated 1949 by NHLR; a 2018 report says 1937)

access.note: Seasonal staffed lookout. The field guide says the staffer is used to visitors and asks that visits be between 9:00 a.m. and 6:00 p.m. No closure or permission requirement appears in these sources; the 2026 season was not confirmed.

visit.trail_note: Lookout road is 0.8 miles to drive. Alternatively walk about half a mile from the Table Rock South Trailhead, leaving the road to climb cross-country after the first patch of forest.

facts.agency: U.S. Forest Service (Wallowa-Whitman National Forest, Unity Ranger District)

events.note: First structure: a cupola house, dated only to the 1920s (NHLR says early 1920s)
An L-4 14 x 14 ft cab with catwalk replaced the cupola; the Forest Lookouts history dates the L-4 cabin to 1936
Roy Weikal and his wife stationed as a new lookout-fireman station, the first season the point was manned
New L-4 completed; NHLR and the Forest Lookouts history give 1949, while a 2018 visit report calls the cab 1937
Lou Maher went into the service and Gary Squires replaced him; firelookout.com lists Lew Maker for 1962
Ten solar panels stolen from the lookout in June; Forest Service offered a reward of up to $1,000
Registered on the National Historic Lookout Register June 1, 1998
Lookout evacuated in July because of the extreme behavior of a fire the observer had reported earlier
Rail Fire reached the summit; the lookout was wrapped in protective foil and survived. Accounts differ on which outbuildings burned
Visit on May 27, 2018 found the lookout staffed for the summer

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The Forest Lookouts history dates the first L-4 cabin to 1936 and the NHLR and firelookout.com date it to 1937. The story gives 1937 as the common date and notes 1936.

NHLR and the Forest Lookouts history record a new L-4 in 1949, while the 2018 visit report and the Oregon Hikers page describe the cab as 1937. The story reports the 1949 date from the register and the history, and flags the 2018 report's 1937.
A 1920s cupola stood on the summit, but the 1939 notice calls 1939 the first season the point was manned. The story reports both: a structure in the 1920s and staffing from 1939.

The Forest Lookouts history says an old outhouse was lost. The Oregon Hikers page says an old wooden garage and the former outhouse burned. The 2018 visit says the lookout and outhouse were wrapped. The story reports the disagreement.
The Forest Lookouts history gives Lou Maher as the man who left the lookout in 1962. firelookout.com lists Lew Maker for 1962. The spelling is unresolved, so the story does not name him.

NHLR gives 7,756 ft (2,364 m), which matches the brief's 2364.0 m. firelookout.com and the 2018 visit give 7,815 ft, and the Forest Lookouts history quotes a Baker City Herald figure of 7,826 ft. Elevation is not stated in the story.
NHLR places the lookout in the Wallowa-Whitman National Forest, firelookout.com says Wallowa-Whitman/Malheur, and Oregon Hikers says Malheur. The story uses the NHLR's Wallowa-Whitman.

notes_for_editor: The brief's Forest Service link (recarea 56921) is a general Umatilla recreation page that does not mention Table Rock, so it was not used. Build dates disagree (1936 vs 1937 for the first L-4; 1949 vs 1937 for the present cab) and the story says so. Current staffing is not confirmed past the 2018 visit and an undated Oregon Hikers page; no 2019 to 2026 staffing source was found, so check the 2026 season before publishing a present-tense staffing claim. No rental or booking source was found. The 2016 Rail Fire outbuilding detail differs between sources and is reported as disputed. The Baker City Herald and 1997 reward are cited only through the Forest Lookouts history, not read directly. Story is about 333 words.
